intro: A maximum attention weight does not describe the full distribution. Entropy and effective support distinguish focused and diffuse rows.
task: Return attention entropy in natural units, exponential effective support, and the largest weight per query.
requirements: attention is a query-by-key nonnegative matrix whose rows sum to one within absolute tolerance 1e-8. Normalize rows after validation.
Return {"entropy": vector, "effective_support": exp(entropy), "peak": row maximum}. Use the convention 0*log(0)=0.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Focused and diffuse
examples.output:
{'entropy': [0.0, 1.09861228867],
 'effective_support': [1.0, 3.0],
 'peak': [1.0, 0.333333333333]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Only positive probabilities contribute to the entropy sum.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: A uniform row over K keys has effective support K; a one-hot row has support one.

explanation: Exponentiating entropy expresses uncertainty on the scale of an equivalent number of uniformly attended keys. This makes distributions with different key counts easier to interpret.
Effective support is a distribution diagnostic rather than a count of exactly nonzero entries. Many tiny weights can coexist with support close to one when nearly all mass is concentrated on one key.
